- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment swings; if sentiment shifts from high to low, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay or use 7-day rolling average to adjust initial values.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day SMA of true values as baseline for correction.
